conviction_note: Two direct truckload peers have spoken since KNX last did. Werner pre-announced Q3 adj EPS of $0.15-0.16 against a $0.36 consensus, with $0.18 of cost headwinds versus Q2 from fuel, driver pay and an insurance reserve. JBHT warned in September and its truckload operating income fell despite revenue per load up 29%. Against that, KNX's own consensus ($0.75) has barely moved, KNX has not pre-announced, and mid-October tender rejections of about 14% support the Q4 guide the stock trades on. The reported quarter therefore leans to a miss against the guide midpoint, while the reaction depends on the Q4 guide and on a stock that is already 23% off its high and sold its last large beat (-4.9%). Hence p_up 47 on an abs move of 5.5. The finding sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (-0.33) differ in sign because the positives are guide- and positioning-sized and the negatives are reported-quarter-sized; the gap is small and that is the honest read.

findings.finding: Werner (WERN) pre-announced Q3 2026 on 2026-10-19, two days before KNX. Adjusted EPS is $0.15-0.16 against a $0.36 consensus and revenue $946-951m against $953.6m expected. Werner quantified about $0.18 per share of cost headwinds versus Q2: rapidly rising fuel prices, driver recruitment and retention spending, and a late-quarter insurance reserve adjustment on past claims. KNX's own Q3 consensus is still $0.75, the midpoint of its $0.71-0.77 guide, and KNX has not pre-announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: KNX sold a large Q2 beat on 2026-07-22 (adj EPS $0.63 against $0.49 consensus and a $0.45-0.49 guide, with the Q3 guide above consensus): -4.88%. On 2025-10-22 it fell -7.13%. Its reported-quarter surprises have not been paid; the guide drives the move.
findings.why_not_priced: KNX's sell-side bar has not absorbed it: Zacks' consensus of $0.75 was down only 1.3% in 60 days as of Oct 15, before Werner spoke. If the market had fully transmitted Werner's 55% miss to KNX, KNX would have fallen on Oct 19-20 and its consensus would sit near the bottom of the guide. Instead KNX is +0.65% over 5 days. Partly priced: WERN itself fell only 1.1% on the warning (it was already 31% off its mid-July peak), and KNX is 23% off its high.
findings.independence: JBHT warned in mid-September of a 5-10% q/q earnings decline on diesel near $6.30 and $25m of added driver costs (https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/jb-hunt-shares-down-13-us-transportation-stocks-have-problems); that is a separate document and is filed as its own finding. KNX's Q2 10-Q flags tightening insurance markets (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001492691/000149269126000059/knx-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: JBHT's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-15): truckload revenue per load rose 29% and segment revenue 37%, yet truckload operating income fell 6% and DCS operating income fell 22%, on purchased transportation, driver pay, insurance and fuel costs. Fuel expense rose to 7.1% of revenue from 5.4%. The CFO said rapid fuel moves 'create a timing mismatch and dilute margins'. Q3 EPS was down 5% q/q, at the better end of the September warning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above: KNX sold its last beat (-4.88%) and fell -7.13% in Oct 2025. JBHT itself traded -2.3% after hours on its print, after a -13% day on the September warning.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and widely read, so it is mostly priced. What remains is that higher price did not convert into truckload margin even at a carrier with record revenue per load, while KNX's guide assumes a 650-750bp y/y improvement in truckload operating ratio. KNX's consensus at the guide midpoint shows the sell side has not carried that across.
findings.independence: Werner's pre-announcement (separate company, separate document) names the same three cost lines. CFO quote: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/10/j-b-hunt-third-quarter-earnings-rise-narrowly-revenue-up-20/

findings.finding: Truckload conditions eased during Q3 after the July 22 guide, which assumed 'current conditions continue with pressured capacity'. SONAR tender rejections fell from a cycle peak above 17.5% around July 4 to about 13.5% at Labor Day. DAT recorded the steepest July-to-August spot decline in its 16-year history, and spot fell below contract by August. September spot linehaul ex-fuel slipped again (van $2.17, -2c m/m) while contract linehaul held ($2.40, -1c). KNX's true spot exposure is in the low-to-mid teens percent of its truckload book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's rapid tightening produced a beat that was sold (-4.88%). No case on file of an easing intra-quarter spot market moving KNX.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry proxy, not a KNX number, and is mostly priced. The residual is that a guide set at the July spot peak embedded spot-exposed revenue that August and September did not deliver. Lower spot also cuts purchased-transportation cost in KNX's Logistics segment (Q2 Logistics OR 96.4% on high purchased-transportation cost), so the net effect is small.
findings.independence: Tender-rejection path: https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=583148 (2026-10-14). Spot exposure 'low-to-mid teens': https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=572459 (2026-04-23).

findings.finding: The SONAR Truckload Rejection Index jumped to 14.17% in mid-October 2026 (FreightWaves, 2026-10-14). That is about three times the 2023-2025 range, comes on a supply shortfall with flat tender volume, and has spot above contract on 38% of the top-50 Los Angeles lanes. It bears on the Q4 guide KNX gives tonight, against a Q4 EPS consensus of about $0.81 that is above the Q3 bar and already assumes further contract repricing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Jul 2026 a Q3 guide above consensus came with -4.88% (on top of a large beat). In Apr 2026 the Q2 guide was reiterated after a Q1 miss and the stock rose +2.8%. In Jan 2026 the Q4 2025 print with a capacity-tightening narrative went +2.61%. The guide line has paid in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: SONAR is widely watched, but the stock has fallen 5.3% in 20 days and broke its 200-day average on Oct 9, i.e. it traded the peer cost warnings and not the October re-tightening. If the market had priced a strong Q4 guide, KNX would not sit 23% off its high with consensus Q3 unchanged. The skew (-3.23, upside paid) and the call-heavy open interest lean the same way, so this agrees with the options and is partly in them.
findings.independence: Schneider's Q2 2026 call described a driver-constrained market, spot testing prior-cycle highs, double-digit renewals and early-stage contract recovery (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/schneider-national-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-31/). KNX in April was targeting high-single to low-double-digit increases on 70% of its book (https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=572459).

findings.finding: KNX's own Q2 2026 release shows truckload plus LTL fuel surcharge revenue of $331.3m against fuel expense of $307.4m, a $24m surplus, versus a roughly $14m deficit in Q2 2025, in a quarter when diesel was already spiking. So KNX's net fuel exposure may differ from Werner's: its LTL fuel surcharge is percentage-based. ODFL's QTD revenue/cwt was +11.3% including fuel against +4.8% excluding it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 fuel and weather cost 5-6c and the stock still rose +2.8% on the reiterated guide; Q2 net fuel was positive and the beat was sold. Fuel has not been a line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The Werner and JBHT read-through treats rising fuel as a uniform carrier headwind. KNX's own filing shows the surcharge out-recovering fuel cost in Q2. If the market had absorbed that, KNX would have decoupled from WERN's 31% drawdown; it is 23% off its high instead. However, Q3's rise was steeper (Aug +10%, Sept +15% retail; one-week surcharge lag), so the Q2 surplus may not repeat, hence the small size.
findings.independence: ODFL August update (https://www.ajot.com/news/old-dominion-freight-line-provides-update-for-third-quarter-2026), showing the LTL fuel-surcharge mechanism. The monthly diesel path cuts the other way (https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=583491).

findings.finding: Short interest rose 42% over the quarter, from 9.3m shares (Jul 31) to 13.2m (Sep 30), about 8% of float, with 3.1 days to cover. Option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.23) and the 25-delta skew is -3.23 (upside paid), so shorts have built into a print where the options lean up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior case on file of a short build ahead of a KNX print; post-print moves ranged -7.13% to +2.80%.
findings.why_not_priced: The short build is itself the market's bearish bet on the peer cost read, and it means part of the reported-quarter miss is positioned for. A guide that holds gives covering fuel; at 3.1 days to cover it is a modest mechanism rather than a squeeze setup.
findings.independence: Option open-interest ratio and skew from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options chain, 2026-10-21) are a separate source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Used Class 8 prices held up into the quarter: ACT reported June average retail $61,751 (+1.5% y/y, +2% m/m), J.D. Power auction prices +14.7% y/y, and an ACT August headline of prices +2.2% on tightening inventories. That supports the $12-17m equipment-gain line in KNX's Q3 guide (gains were a 5c y/y tailwind in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gains on sale have not been cited as a driver of any KNX reaction on file.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company guided ($12-17m), so it is mostly expected; sized near zero accordingly.
findings.independence: Fleet Equipment ACT headline for August, a teaser only (https://www.fleetequipmentmag.com/used-truck-sales-climb-august/).

findings.finding: KNX's Q2 2026 10-Q warns that 'with significant tightening in the insurance markets' it may see changes in premiums and retention limits. KNX took 8c of adverse LTL claim development in Q1 2026, and Werner booked a late-Q3 reserve adjustment on past claims. That leaves a risk of a claims or reserve charge in KNX's Q3 adjusted numbers that the guide did not include.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (8c claims hit, adj EPS $0.09 against $0.25 consensus) still drew +2.8% because the Q2 guide was reiterated. A claims hit has not been decisive for this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a risk-factor sentence, not a quantified charge. A charge would be visible only tonight. Partly overlaps the Werner finding (same insurance-reserve mechanism), so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Shares the insurance theme with Werner's 2026-10-19 release (finding 1); not independent of it in kind. Q1 claims hit: https://www.freightwaves.com/?p=572459

baseline_tension: The peer cost warnings point down on the reported quarter while the skew (-3.23, upside paid), call-heavy open interest and October tightness point up for the guide. The stock's 23% drawdown and -5.3% 20-day run-up suggest the cost read is largely in the price, so the evidence leaves p_up near 50 rather than cutting hard against the options.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning/skew): Werner peer-miss negative shrunk from -1.5 to -1.2 because its sign runs against an upside-paid skew and a rising (not crowded) short build.
Rules 5 and 9 (proxy; net of the rest): the spot-easing finding shrunk from -0.8 to -0.4 because it is an industry proxy and lower spot also cuts KNX Logistics' purchased-transportation cost.
Rule 1 (reaction history sells beats) moved p_up from 46 toward 50 (to 47), since the reported-quarter negatives land on a line this stock has not traded on.
Rule 6: bar confirmed against the company guide plus two agreeing consensus sources ($0.75); the Q4 bar ($0.81) has one source, so the guidance finding stays capped at +1.5.
Left standing: the JBHT, fuel-offset, positioning, used-truck and insurance findings, whose sizes the file did not change.
